sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AnythingLLM is an all-in-one AI app for chatting with your documents and running AI agents. You connect a local or cloud language model, add your files, and get a private ChatGPT-style workspace, as a desktop app or a self-hosted Docker server.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building a private document chatbot usually means wiring together a model, embeddings, a vector database and a UI. AnythingLLM bundles all of that, runs locally by default, and supports multiple users when self-hosted.
whoFor: People who want a private ChatGPT over their own documents
Teams self-hosting a multi-user AI workspace
Local model users (Ollama, LM Studio and others)
Developers who want an API and embeddable chat widget
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an easy, polished, local-first document chat and agent app. Multi-user permissions and the website chat widget need the Docker version.
requirements: Desktop app: Mac, Windows or Linux
Docker version: Docker, with at least 2 GB RAM and about 10 GB disk recommended on cloud servers
Access to an LLM, local or remote

overview: AnythingLLM lets you create workspaces, upload documents like PDF, TXT and DOCX by drag and drop, and chat with them with source citations. Agents inside workspaces can browse the web and more. It works with popular closed and open-source LLM providers, embedding models, speech models and vector databases.

By default it uses a built-in LanceDB vector database and embeds text privately on the instance. The Docker version adds multi-user support with permissions and an embeddable chat widget for websites; there's also white-labelling, a developer API and a browser extension.

You can install the desktop app, run the Docker image, or deploy to AWS, GCP, DigitalOcean, Render, Railway and others. The app collects anonymous telemetry, which you can turn off with DISABLE_TELEMETRY or in the Privacy settings.

install.verificationNote: Commands come from AnythingLLM's README and Docker guide. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Run with local storage
steps.body: Mounting storage on the host lets you update without losing data.
steps.code:
export STORAGE_LOCATION=$HOME/anythingllm && \
mkdir -p $STORAGE_LOCATION && \
touch "$STORAGE_LOCATION/.env" && \
docker run -d --rm -p 3001:3001 \
--cap-add SYS_ADMIN \
-v ${STORAGE_LOCATION}:/app/server/storage \
-v ${STORAGE_LOCATION}/.env:/app/server/.env \
-e STORAGE_DIR="/app/server/storage" \
mintplexlabs/anythingllm

steps.title: Run with local storage
steps.code:
$env:STORAGE_LOCATION="$HOME\Documents\anythingllm"; `
If(!(Test-Path $env:STORAGE_LOCATION)) {New-Item $env:STORAGE_LOCATION -ItemType Directory}; `
If(!(Test-Path "$env:STORAGE_LOCATION\.env")) {New-Item "$env:STORAGE_LOCATION\.env" -ItemType File}; `
docker run -d --rm -p 3001:3001 `
--cap-add SYS_ADMIN `
-v "$env:STORAGE_LOCATION`:/app/server/storage" `
-v "$env:STORAGE_LOCATION\.env:/app/server/.env" `
-e STORAGE_DIR="/app/server/storage" `
mintplexlabs/anythingllm;

troubleshooting.problem: Can't reach Ollama, LM Studio or Chroma on localhost from Docker
troubleshooting.solution: Use http://host.docker.internal:PORT; on Linux add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway to docker run.

troubleshooting.problem: Lost data after updating the container
troubleshooting.solution: Mount the storage folder on the host as in the install command.
Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY to true, or turn it off under Privacy in the sidebar.
